script: Find a comfortable position. Feel the support beneath your body. Breathe in slowly through your nose. Notice the air entering. Let it out without rushing. script: Close your eyes if that feels comfortable. Notice your forehead and let it soften. Release your jaw. Allow your shoulders to lower. Feel your hands resting. protocol.evidence: VA describes this technique and relaxation research. This brief four-group adaptation is neither the full protocol nor a clinically validated session.
protocol.safety: Use little effort and breathe normally. Skip painful or injured areas. With significant injuries, spasms or back problems, consult a clinician before tensing muscles.

source.name: VA Whole Health · Progressive Muscle Relaxation

steps.text: Sit or lie comfortably. You will gently tense and release, without holding your breath. You may simply imagine the release instead.
Hands: gently curl your fingers.
Open your hands. Notice the difference between tension and rest.
Arms: bend your elbows and tense gently.
Release your arms and let them rest. Notice sensations without demanding relaxation.
Shoulders: lift them a little without straining your neck.
Let your shoulders lower and notice the support beneath you.
Feet: gently point your toes, only if comfortable.
Release your feet. Let your legs rest. Breathe naturally.
Notice your whole body. Take a few moments to move and return to your surroundings.

protocol.safety: Keep eyes open and watch your path. Do not use while driving, in traffic, on stairs or near obstacles. You may practice seated.

steps.text: Choose a level route without traffic or obstacles. Keep eyes open, volume low and attention on your surroundings. You may also practice seated, noticing your feet.
Begin walking at a comfortable pace. Notice one foot touching the ground, then the other. No need to match steps with breathing or change your natural walk.
Widen attention to colors, sounds and your direction. Your surroundings come first. If obstacles or people approach, pause the practice and attend to your path.
When your mind wanders, return to one step and the space ahead. Notice arm movement or shifting support if you wish. Walking itself is enough.
Stop in a safe place. Notice your resting feet and look around. Then choose to continue your walk or return to your activity.

protocol.evidence: An original story inspired by guided imagery and relaxation used in sophrology practices. Not a validated clinical protocol.
protocol.safety: Imagine only what feels comfortable. You may keep your eyes open. If distress arises, stop and notice your surroundings.

steps.text: Find comfortable support. Notice where your body rests. There is no need to change your breathing. Imagine Lumi has found a little path beside the sea and invites you to explore it, without hurry.
The path reaches a cove. You choose how far to stay from the water. The sand may be warm or cool; let the scene take colors that suit you. If you prefer, simply listen to the soundscape.
A wave arrives and recedes. You do not need to match it with your breath. Simply notice movement and the space between movements. Lumi sits beside you, content that nothing needs solving right now.
Imagine your shoulders can rest a little more. Your hands rest like smooth pebbles on the sand. A thought may appear. Let it be there and return to a simple detail in the scene.
The horizon remains, asking nothing of you. Choose a word to carry with you: space, lightness, pause, or another that comes. You need not feel anything special. This moment may be enough.
Lumi gets up slowly. The cove can remain in your imagination as you return to your body’s real supports. Move your fingers, notice where you are and return to your day in your own time.

steps.text: Settle your body and notice your feet’s support. Imagine a garden seen from a covered porch. You can stay where you are. Lumi watches the leaves, and soft rain fills the spaces between sounds.
Choose an imagined leaf. A drop rests at its tip before falling. There is no right way to see the scene; it can be an idea, a color or simply a sound.
Feel your hands resting. If you wish, let your fingers soften. Each plant occupies its place without needing to grow faster. You too can allow a few moments without performance.
Lumi finds a sheltered bench. Imagine sitting and watching light shift on the leaves. Breathe naturally. When you notice distraction, return to a sound without scolding your wandering mind.
The imagined rain grows more distant. Choose one small kindness after this pause: drink water, stretch comfortably or simply leave a space before the next task.
The garden can wait for another visit. Notice your body’s real weight and the sounds where you are. Move your hands and feet slowly. Take only what makes sense for you today.
